output:
**Subject: Re: Saturday alarm**

Kristen,

Here’s the straight story. It was my popcorn, and it was my fault. It wasn’t the microwave.

Saturday, Nov. 7, around 10:40, I put a bag of butter popcorn in the break room microwave, hit the popcorn button, and went back out front. A customer needed a shear pin for his snowblower, and finding the right one took longer than I expected—probably six or seven minutes. That’s when the popcorn burned and the alarm went off.

We cleared the store for about 25 minutes. The engine from up on Hertel came, and there was no damage, just smoke and a terrible smell. I know that doesn’t make it a small thing. We had customers standing outside in 30-degree weather, and I feel especially bad about the Hendersons leaving a full cart. Knowing them, they’ll be back, but that doesn’t make it right.

I’ll cover Northpoint’s $175 bill. You can take it out of my check or I can bring you cash, whichever is easier for you. I’ll also get Denise her coffee. Standing by the propane cage without a coat was above and beyond answering an alarm.

For the record, the September alarm was the sensor in the paint aisle, not me. I’m only mentioning that so the two reports don’t get tangled together, not to dodge Saturday. Saturday is on me.

I’d ask you and Gary to please keep me on Saturdays. I like the weekend crowd, and I need the hours with heating oil season here. You have my word there will be no repeat. I’m done with microwave popcorn at the store.

After 31 years on the job, I finally get my first alarm as a civilian over a bag of popcorn. Of course Mikey Szymanski was on the engine—I broke him in as a probie back in ’03, so I’ll never hear the end of it. My wife said the van smelled like a burnt movie theater, so I caught it at home too.

Sorry, Kristen. Just tell me how you want the $175 handled.

Walt
